title: Mapping Memory, Mapping Meals: A Deep-Mapped 3D WebGIS Archive of Indigenous Foodways and Cultural Heritage in West Bengal
description:
Mapping Memory, Mapping Meals is an open-access interactive 3D WebGIS archive documenting the foodways, culinary memory, and ecological knowledge of tribal and indigenous communities in West Bengal, India. The archive holds 97 geocoded food entries across communities including the Santal, Toto, Rajbangshi, Mech, Lodha, Rabha, Garo, Kheria Sabar, Oraon, Gorkha, Limbu, Bhutia, and Birhor, among others.

Each entry is organized across 14 knowledge layers covering ecological setting, community affiliation, ethnobotanical data, culinary technology, temporal and scarcity context, oral tradition, archival sources, erased traditions, sacred foods, medicinal knowledge, cultural significance, geo-location, image references, and historical origins (L1-L14, with L14 spanning seven sub-categories). The layering holds the complexity of food as a cultural object without flattening it into any single discipline.

Tribal food documentation in West Bengal has been largely confined to ethnobotanical surveys and nutritional studies. Integrated cultural and historical accounts remain thin. The archive responds to this gap by treating food as a site of memory, oral tradition, and community identity rather than as a resource variable alone.

The archive runs as a static deep map inside the project website, built on MapLibre GL JS over 3D terrain with dark, daylight and satellite basemaps. Users can filter entries by community, knowledge layer, or region. Version 2 adds narrated Talking Tours, map Snapshots, per-entry citations and a community Guestbook for visitors' food memories.

This project is part of HS02: Mapping of Regional Cuisines, Food and Cultural Studies at the Indian Institute of Space Science and Technology (IIST), Thiruvananthapuram. A conference paper, Culinary Cartographies of Memory: Deep Mapping Indigenous Foodways and Cultural Heritage in West Bengal, was presented at the World Folklore Day Celebrations 2026, University of Hyderabad (20-23 August 2026).

Live archive: https://mappingmemorymappingmeals.github.io/IIST/map.html
Project site: https://mappingmemorymappingmeals.github.io/IIST/
